question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(2,7,20)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨6,-9,3⟩=51.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨6,-9,3⟩ & =51 \\ 6x-9y+3z & =51 \\ 3z & =51-6x+9y \\ z & =17-2x+3y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=1$ and $y=2,$ we get 

$$
z=17-2(1)+3(2)=21.
$$

So, the point $Q(1,2,21)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,21⟩-⟨2,7,20⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨6,-9,3⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 6+(-5)\cdot (-9)+1\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-9)^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+45+3|}{\sqrt{36+81+9}} \\  & =\frac{|42|}{\sqrt{126}} \\  & =\sqrt{14}\end{aligned}
$$
